newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Senate reduces uncertainty over '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Polish Senate reduces uncertainty over '97 budget.

text.p: The Polish Senate's decision to cut personal income tax levels next year by one point reduces uncertainty over the probable 1997 budget deficit, now likely to be near this year's 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

The Senate on Thursday amended the lower house's income tax bill and introduced levels at 20, 32 and 44 percent in 1997, slightly higher than those proposed by the government and defeated in the lower house late last month.

Deputy Finance Minister Waldemar Manugiewicz told Reuters that if the Senate decision came into force, the government would amend its current budget draft to accommodate lower tax revenues and a higher deficit of about 2.8 percent of GDP.

"If the Senate's decision becomes law then, obviously, the deficit will increase by about 850-900 million zlotys to 2.8 percent of GDP from 2.6 percent assumed by the current draft," Manugiewicz said.
He said budget expenditures would remain unchanged, and the higher deficit would be financed by increased revenues from privatisation of banks and sales of government paper abroad.
He also said some of the cash left in consumers' pockets due to lower taxes would return to the treasury's coffers as indirect taxes, such as Value Added Tax (VAT) and excise tax.

The Senate amendments now return to the lower house, which can either adopt them or uphold its proposal for a four-level tax scale, granting sharp tax cuts for people on low incomes, which the government has deemed economically unsound.

If the lower house were to reaffirm this four-level scale, President Aleksander Kwasniewski, linked to the ruling coalition's larger party the Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), has suggested he would veto the bill.

His veto would in effect keep the present 21-, 33- and 45-percent tax levels intact and the 1997 budget unchanged from the government draft, now being debated in parliament, which assumes no tax cuts and a deficit of 2.6 percent of GDP.
But the Senate amendments appear set to survive the lower house vote after the main opposition party, the Union for Freedom, indicated it would support them, along with the SLD.
"I confirm that the Union (for Freedom) will vote in favour of this scale," party chairman Leszek Balcerowicz said.
Last month, UW deputies joined other opposition members and the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL) to push through the four-level tax scale, a move that stunned the government.
With the UW, the SLD, which backed the one-point tax reduction, can muster more than the 50 percent of votes in the lower house needed to uphold the Senate decision.
Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko welcomed the Senate vote, saying the amended bill fit in broadly with government plans. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
